definitions.explanation: An amphibian that lives both in water and on land, known for its jumping ability and croaking sound.

examples.japanese: ⟦{田|た}んぼ→田んぼ：00402_tanbo⟧⟦で→で：00502_de⟧{蛙|かえる}⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{鳴|な}いている→鳴く：04388_naku⟧。
examples.english: Frogs are croaking in the rice paddy.

examples.japanese: {蛙|かえる}⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{池|いけ}→池：00848_ike⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{飛|と}び{込|こ}んだ→飛び込む：04614_tobikomu⟧。
examples.english: A frog jumped into the pond.
examples.notes: This echoes Matsuo Bashō's famous haiku

examples.japanese: ⟦{子供|こども}→子供：00554_kodomo⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{頃|ころ}→〜ころ：03091_koro⟧、⟦よく→よく：00601_yoku⟧{蛙|かえる}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{捕|つか}まえて→捕まえる：01214_tsukamaeru⟧⟦{遊|あそ}んだ→遊ぶ：00550_asobu⟧。
examples.english: When I was a child, I often played by catching frogs.

examples.japanese: ⟦{夏|なつ}→夏：02236_natsu⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{夜|よる}→夜：00487_yoru⟧、⟦{田|た}んぼ→田んぼ：00402_tanbo⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{近|ちか}く→近く：00923_chikaku⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{歩|ある}く→歩く：00538_aruku⟧⟦と→と：00512_to⟧{蛙|かえる}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{合唱|がっしょう}→合唱：04900_gasshou⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{聞|き}こえる→聞こえる：01229_kikoeru⟧。
examples.english: On summer nights, you can hear a chorus of frogs when walking near the rice paddies.
examples.notes: {蛙|かえる}の{合唱|がっしょう} = chorus of frogs

examples.english: The proverb 'a frog's child is a frog' is used to mean that children take after their parents.

notes:
{蛙|かえる} refers to frogs in general, sometimes also including toads.

Alternative kanji: {蛙|かわず} (literary/poetic reading)

Common expressions:
- {蛙|かえる}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{子|こ}→子：09851_ko⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧{蛙|かえる} (like father, like son; literally "a frog's child is a frog")
- {井|い}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{中|なか}→中：00654_naka⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{蛙|かわず}⟦{大海|たいかい}→大海：29270_taikai⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{知|し}らず→知る：00458_shiru⟧ (a frog in a well knows nothing of the great ocean - narrow-minded person)
- {蛙|かえる}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{合唱|がっしょう}→合唱：04900_gasshou⟧ (chorus of frogs)

Counter: ⟦{匹|ひき}→匹：00939_hiki⟧

Cultural note:
{蛙|かえる} is a homophone of ⟦{帰|かえ}る→帰る：00508_kaeru⟧ (to return), so frog charms are popular as good luck items for safe returns. Matsuo Bashō's famous haiku about a frog jumping into a pond ({古池|ふるいけ}や{蛙|かわず}⟦{飛|と}び{込|こ}む→飛び込む：04614_tobikomu⟧⟦{水|みず}→水：02258_mizu⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{音|おと}→音：00743_oto⟧) is one of the most well-known poems in Japanese literature.
